tokens.name: background
tokens.usage: The page itself. Pair with foreground.

tokens.name: foreground
tokens.usage: Default body text and icons on background.

tokens.name: card
tokens.usage: Raised surfaces: cards, panels, sheets. Pair with card-foreground.

tokens.name: card-foreground
tokens.usage: Text on card.

tokens.name: popover
tokens.usage: Overlays: dropdowns, tooltips, menus. Mirrors card.

tokens.name: popover-foreground
tokens.usage: Text on popover.

tokens.name: primary
tokens.usage: The single main action in a view. Pair with primary-foreground. Note it steps DARKER in dark mode, which is faithful to the reference.

tokens.name: primary-foreground
tokens.usage: Labels and icons on primary. 5.9:1 light, 7.6:1 dark.

tokens.name: secondary
tokens.usage: Supporting actions beside a primary one. The one token on a zinc (cool) ramp; everything else is neutral.

tokens.name: secondary-foreground
tokens.usage: Text on secondary.

tokens.name: muted
tokens.usage: De-emphasised fills: inactive rows, disabled surfaces, skeletons.

tokens.name: muted-foreground
tokens.usage: Secondary text: captions, help text, table meta. 4.74:1 light, so body-size is fine but do not go below 14px.

tokens.name: accent
tokens.usage: Hover and active states on neutral surfaces. Currently equal to muted; kept separate so the two can diverge.

tokens.name: accent-foreground
tokens.usage: Text on accent.

tokens.name: destructive
tokens.usage: Delete, revoke and other irreversible actions. DERIVED, not extracted, and only AA-large (4.36:1 light, 3.48:1 dark) - acceptable for 14px+ semibold button labels, not for small text. Because the brand is red, this reads close to primary; a non-red destructive is the stronger option if delete actions must be unmistakable.

tokens.name: destructive-foreground
tokens.usage: Labels on destructive.

tokens.name: border
tokens.usage: Hairlines and dividers. Deliberately low contrast (1.26:1) - a boundary, never an outline carrying meaning on its own.

tokens.name: input
tokens.usage: Form field fills. A translucent wash, not a solid, so it composites over both card and background.

tokens.name: muted-subtle
tokens.usage: `muted` at 50%. The fill for a row or disclosure item on a card - ListGroup rows, Accordion items, settings rows. One step lighter than `muted`, which keeps a stack of rows from reading as a wall of grey.

tokens.name: track
tokens.usage: The empty half of a slider, and the fill of an unchecked checkbox or radio - the off state of a control. A third alpha ramp, distinct from both border and input.

tokens.name: ring
tokens.usage: Focus rings only. DERIVED, not extracted - the reference draws no focus state. Clears 3:1 on every neutral surface in both modes (dark: 5.20:1 on background, 3.97:1 on muted). MUST be used with ring-offset: on a primary or destructive button the ring and the surface are both red, so without the offset gap it is invisible.

tokens.name: ring-offset
tokens.usage: The gap between a control and its focus ring, tracking background so the ring sits on the page rather than on the control. DERIVED. Standard usage is a 2px ring with a 2px offset.

tokens.name: chart-1
tokens.usage: Lightest step of the data ramp. First series, or lowest value.

tokens.name: chart-2
tokens.usage: Second data series.

tokens.name: chart-3
tokens.usage: Third data series.

tokens.name: chart-4
tokens.usage: Fourth data series. Equal to primary in light mode.

tokens.name: chart-5
tokens.usage: Darkest step of the data ramp. Adjacent chart steps separate by only 1.25-1.35:1, so for 4-5 categorical series add shape, pattern or direct labels rather than relying on colour.

styles.name: display
styles.usage: The one big figure on a card: a balance, a goal total. Carries tabular numerals.

styles.name: heading
styles.usage: Largest card title. One per card at most.

styles.name: title
styles.usage: Stat values and prominent section titles (3.4 kW, May 25 2024). Drop to weight 500 with letterSpacing -0.45px for centred empty-state titles, which is how the reference sets them.

styles.name: body
styles.usage: Introductory and supporting copy under a title.

styles.name: text
styles.usage: The default. Table cells, list rows, descriptions, most interface text.

styles.name: prose
styles.usage: Long-form paragraphs that run several lines. NOTE the fractional line height: the reference sets 162.5%, which lands on 22.75px at 14px. Round to 23px, or normalise to 24px for a 4px grid.

styles.name: label
styles.usage: Form field labels and switch titles. NOTE the fractional line height: 137.5% lands on 19.25px. Round to 19px, or use 20px to match text.

styles.name: button
styles.usage: All button and tab labels, at every button height.

styles.name: caption
styles.usage: Help text, timestamps, chart axis labels.

styles.name: eyebrow
styles.usage: Small uppercase label above a title (RETIREMENT, UPCOMING, COVER ART).

styles.name: code
styles.usage: Identifiers and keys: env var names, token names.

styles.name: code-value
styles.usage: The value beside a code key, set in muted-foreground.

styles.name: numeric
styles.usage: Figures in usage meters and dense tables, where digits must align in a column.

radius.note: Eight values, measured across ALL FOUR content artboards. The first pass swept only D5-0 (the app screens) and so missed 6px and 14px entirely, and wrongly recorded 8px as incidental. These are not a scale - 5, 6, 8, 10, 14, 18, 24 have no consistent ratio - so they are named by pixel value, as spacing is. The two exceptions are `pill` and `full`, which name a shape intent rather than a size.

tokens.name: radius-5
tokens.usage: Checkboxes, and nothing else. The only square-ish control in the system.

tokens.name: radius-6
tokens.usage: Chart bars. Used on the weekday bars of the activity charts; ~28 occurrences, all in data visualisation.

tokens.name: radius-8
tokens.usage: Small tiles: colour swatches, compact grid cells. Widely used on the showcase boards - the first extraction called this incidental, which was wrong.

tokens.name: radius-10
tokens.usage: Inner tiles inside a card: transaction icon squares, stat blocks.

tokens.name: radius-14
tokens.usage: 40x40 icon tiles, small bordered cards, chart tooltips, and 24px icon buttons. At 40px this reads as a rounded square rather than a circle, which is what distinguishes it from `pill`.

tokens.name: radius-pill
tokens.usage: Every interactive control - buttons, inputs, textareas, badges, tabs, switches, slider tracks and thumbs. At the system's control heights (20/28/32px) 18px exceeds half the height, so it renders as a true pill. This is the system's defining shape; anything else on a control will look wrong.

tokens.name: radius-24
tokens.usage: Cards, panels, sheets, dialogs. The outer container radius.

tokens.name: radius-full
tokens.usage: Circles: radio dots, avatars, status dots.

spacing.note: Eleven steps, measured across the whole light artboard. This is a 2px grid, not a 4px one - 2, 6, 10 and 14 are all in real use. Tokens are named by their pixel value (space-2 ... space-40); each carries its Tailwind step in `tailwindStep`, because every step maps exactly onto Tailwind's own scale. Naming by pixel rather than by step is deliberate: step names are fractional (0.5, 1.5, 2.5) and a '.' is not valid in a CSS custom-property identifier without escaping, which makes var(--space-1.5) a footgun. 32px (Tailwind's 8) is absent: the scale jumps 24 -> 40.

tokens.name: space-2
tokens.usage: Badge inner block padding, and the tightest icon rows.

tokens.name: space-4
tokens.usage: Icon-to-label gap inside a small button or badge.

tokens.name: space-6
tokens.usage: Icon-to-label gap in a standard button; title-to-subtitle in a card header.

tokens.name: space-8
tokens.usage: Table cell padding; gaps in a tight stack of related controls.

tokens.name: space-10
tokens.usage: Inner padding of an input or textarea. Rare as a gap - two uses on the whole artboard.

tokens.name: space-12
tokens.usage: Horizontal padding inside every button, at all three heights.

tokens.name: space-14
tokens.usage: Vertical padding of a bordered settings row.

tokens.name: space-16
tokens.usage: Horizontal padding of a bordered row; gap between grouped controls.

tokens.name: space-20
tokens.usage: The card unit. Every card's inner padding and the gap between its header, body and footer.

tokens.name: space-24
tokens.usage: Gap between distinct sections inside one card.

tokens.name: space-40
tokens.usage: Largest separation - between major blocks, and the artboard's own gutter.

shadow.note: Six levels, measured across ALL FOUR content artboards. The first pass swept only D5-0 and missed both `hairline` (the most-used level of all) and `overlay`. Each level that carries a drop shadow is a Tailwind shadow with a 1px hairline ring in front of it. The ring is the part that carries the system's look: surfaces are defined by a crisp edge, with the drop doing very little.

tokens.name: shadow-none
tokens.usage: Inputs, textareas and other controls that sit flush in a surface. The reference gives these no shadow at all - they are distinguished by their fill, not by lift.

tokens.name: shadow-hairline
tokens.usage: A 1px ring in the border colour with no drop at all - the most-used elevation in the system (~50 occurrences across both themes). Use it wherever an element needs an edge but no lift: swatch tiles, chart cells, bordered grid items. It is a border that costs no layout, which is why it is a shadow and not a border.

tokens.name: shadow-card
tokens.usage: Every card and panel. Its ring is a near-black/near-white alpha rather than the solid border colour `hairline` uses.

tokens.name: shadow-thumb
tokens.usage: The knob of a switch, and the active tab in a tab track. Same drops as card, with no ring - it sits on a coloured or filled track, where a hairline would read as a seam.

tokens.name: shadow-raised
tokens.usage: Slider thumbs. An element that floats just off the surface it controls. Its ring does not vary by theme.

tokens.name: shadow-overlay
tokens.usage: Anything that floats above the page: chart tooltips in the reference, and by extension dropdown panels, popovers, menus and date pickers. Pairs with radius-14, which is what the reference's tooltip uses - NOT radius-24, which is for cards.
